conj:diophantine-birthday:
Conjecture Algebraic vs transcendental numbers are separated by birthday trajectory. Archimedean specialisation. Liouville's theorem and Roth's theorem bound the approximability of an algebraic irrational by rationals: if \alpha is algebraic of degree d, then |\alpha - p/q| > c/q^d for sufficiently large q (Liouville), and Roth improves the exponent to 2 + \delta for any \delta > 0. Use \delta rather than \varepsilon here to avoid collision with the surreal infinitesimal \varepsilon = 1/\omega used elsewhere in this appendix.

These are analytic statements about approximation rates. The surreal framework suggests a direct algebraic shadow. Algebraic and transcendental numbers distinguish themselves by the birthday trajectory of their sign sequences (birthday grading).

Setup

Every real number \alpha \in \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbf{No} has a canonical sign sequence s_\alpha : \alpha_{\mathrm{birth}} \to \{+, -\} with \alpha_{\mathrm{birth}} = b(\alpha). For reals, b(\alpha) \leq \omega (since \mathbb{R} embeds in the birthday-\leq\omega subfield of \mathbf{No}).

Define the birthday trajectory of \alpha as the function

  b_\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N},
  \qquad b_\alpha(n) := \text{minimum birthday of}~p/q~\text{with}~q \leq n,~|\alpha - p/q|~\text{minimal}.

This serves as the birthday analogue of the classical continued-fraction convergent sequence. Two regimes bracket the behaviour. A quadratic irrational has an eventually periodic continued fraction, limiting its birthday trajectory to logarithmic growth. In contrast, a Liouville number has unboundedly growing partial quotients, forcing a trajectory that climbs toward \omega.

Conjecture

Conjecture (Algebraic-transcendental discrimination via birthday trajectory). The birthday trajectory discriminates algebraic from transcendental numbers:

  1. Algebraic rigidity: if \alpha is algebraic of degree d, then b_\alpha(n) = O(\log n) up to a bounded error. The trajectory grows logarithmically because rational approximations must be explicitly constructed via integer linear algebra (Liouville-type).

  2. Transcendental depth: if \alpha is transcendental (of "generic" type, e.g. Liouville number), b_\alpha(n) grows super-logarithmically, potentially approaching \omega for Liouville-class numbers.

  3. Roth threshold: Roth's exponent 2 + \delta corresponds to the ordinal stratum at which any single \delta > 0 allows non-trivial birthday-trajectory growth for algebraic numbers — finite, bounded birthday depth.

  4. Continued fraction correspondence: the k-th convergent of the continued-fraction expansion of \alpha has birthday exactly \sum_{j \leq k} b(a_j) where a_j are the partial quotients. For algebraic \alpha, \{a_j\} is bounded (by Lagrange for quadratic irrationals, conjecturally for all algebraic); for transcendental \alpha, a_j may grow unboundedly.

Naturality of the construction

Surreal construction is exactly the continued-fraction-like recursive construction of reals:

  • Finite sign sequences = dyadic rationals.
  • Infinite sign sequences = limit reals.
  • The rate at which birthday-depth accumulates per unit of approximation error is a direct measure of how "hard to approximate" a real number is.

Classical diophantine approximation theory measures this rate analytically (via |\alpha - p/q|). The surreal framework measures it algebraically (via birthday trajectory).

Both are studying the same object: how efficiently rationals approach a real.

Conjectural consequences

  1. New proof strategy for Roth's theorem: Roth's theorem becomes a statement about the birthday-growth rate of algebraic sign sequences. A purely algebraic proof (avoiding the Thue-Siegel method) might be accessible.

  2. Liouville-number detection: a number is Liouville if its birthday trajectory approaches \omega; this is an algebraic characterisation, independent of the choice of approximation exponent.

  3. Classification of transcendence types: Mahler's S, T, U classification corresponds to different ordinal strata of birthday trajectories. Elements of U (Liouville-type) live at birthday approaching \omega; elements of S (generic transcendentals) at stabilising finite birthdays.

  4. QOU aether parameter q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps): the conjectured value (not known to be algebraic or transcendental) has a specific birthday trajectory. If computable, this would decide its algebraic status.

Specialisation to QOU

The aether parameter q_0 is the observed aether value at the point of observation; it is extracted by a canonical categorical procedure (via fibre-functor rigidity, Tannaka-Krein, etc.) but its numerical value is empirical. The conjecture predicts:

  • if q_0 is algebraic, its birthday trajectory b_{q_0}(n) is logarithmic (bounded continued-fraction partial quotients, per Lagrange/Roth);
  • if transcendental, the trajectory grows super-logarithmically (approaching Liouville-class behaviour for certain exponentials);
  • which trajectory class q_0 lives in encodes the paper's "algebraic complexity".

Note. Every real number has birthday exactly \omega (the dyadic rationals have finite birthday; every other real has birthday \omega since it is the limit of a length-\omega sign sequence). The algebraic/transcendental distinction therefore cannot be read off the birthday of q_0 itself, only off the growth rate of its rational-approximation trajectory.

Computing q_0's actual birthday trajectory would:

  • decide its algebraic status (open in this paper);
  • give a birthday-based characterisation of the QOU aether.

Proof strategy

Reduction to continued fractions (provable now, modulo the algebraicity conjecture):

  1. The birthday of a dyadic rational p/2^k is k + b(p) \leq k + \log_2 |p|.

  2. For an irrational real \alpha, the birthday trajectory is related to the continued-fraction expansion via: b(\alpha^{(k)}) = \sum_{j \leq k} b(a_j) where \alpha^{(k)} is the k-th convergent.

  3. For quadratic irrationals (Lagrange), \{a_j\} is eventually periodic, so b(\alpha^{(k)}) = O(k) and the birthday trajectory is linear in k, while the approximation quality is O(1/q^2), giving b_\alpha(n) = O(\log n).

  4. For higher algebraic degree: use Roth's theorem to get |\alpha - p/q| > c/q^{2+\delta}, which bounds the continued-fraction partial quotients by a power of k, giving b_\alpha(n) = O((\log n)^{1 + \delta'}) — still poly-log.

  5. For Liouville numbers: |\alpha - p/q| < 1/q^n for every n; this corresponds to unboundedly-growing partial quotients, giving b_\alpha(n) super-polynomial.

Required infrastructure:

  • The continued-fraction expansion machinery.
  • The birthday function of rationals.
  • Roth's theorem.

Falsification path: find an algebraic number whose birthday trajectory grows super-logarithmically. This would either:

  • refute the conjecture, or
  • refute Roth's theorem (unlikely).

Conversely, find a transcendental number with logarithmic birthday trajectory and bounded continued-fraction quotients — this would refute conjecture (2).

Provability assessment: structurally clean once continued- fraction \leftrightarrow birthday bijection is established. The deep content (distinguishing algebraic from transcendental) depends on Roth's theorem, which is deep but classical.

Discussion

Open, but the reduction to continued fractions is classical. The conjecture restates Roth / Liouville in surreal-combinatorial language.

The application to q_0 is the novel part. If q_0 has a computable closed-form birthday, the conjecture characterizes the algebraic complexity of the aether parameter.
thm:diophantine-birthday-trajectory:
Theorem The birthday-trajectory separation: impossible at the birthday, unobstructed at the trajectory, and blocked only by a quantifier. Archimedean specialisation. ## What "separated by birthday trajectory" can and cannot mean

The appendix carries a conjecture that algebraic and transcendental numbers are separated by birthday trajectory, motivated by Liouville and Roth. Taken literally as a statement about the birthday of the number, it is not open — it is impossible.

The axiom \mathrm{birthday}(\iota r) \le \omega places every real, algebraic and transcendental alike, inside [0,\omega]. In Conway's surreals the collapse is total: the dyadic rationals are born strictly before day \omega and every other real is born exactly on day \omega, so

  \mathrm{birthday}(\sqrt{2}) \;=\; \omega \;=\; \mathrm{birthday}(\pi).

Two numbers with equal birthday are indistinguishable to every predicate of the birthday, so no criterion phrased in \mathrm{birthday} \circ \iota can separate them, however cleverly chosen.

The conjecture's own wording already said where to look. Trajectory is load-bearing: Liouville and Roth are about how fast rationals approximate \alpha, which in surreal terms is the shape of the sign expansion — the path — not the ordinal at which it terminates.

The obstruction does not transfer

Moving to trajectories invites the same collapse a second time. Two reals whose sign expansions share a tail differ by a dyadic rational, so any criterion that is a function of the trajectory must be invariant under adding a rational. That is exactly the kind of blanket invariance which flattened the birthday version.

It survives, and for a reason that is a theorem:

criterion invariant under the ambiguity constant on the irrationals
\mathrm{birthday} \circ \iota — yes — separates nothing
\mathrm{LiouvilleWith}\ p yes no — separates

Approximability to order p is invariant under a rational shift and takes both truth values. So the redirection moves to a criterion that survives the invariance its own encoding forces.

⚠ Two things the conjecture's framing gets wrong

One direction is already a theorem. Liouville's theorem — a real approximable to every order is transcendental — is a classical theorem, with \sum 2^{-n!} as a concrete example. Presenting the separation as wholly open overstates what is open.

Roth does not help, though the motivation cites it. Roth sharpens the direction that is already closed: an algebraic irrational has approximation exponent exactly 2, so approximability to any order p>2 already forces transcendence, improving Liouville's degree-dependent bound. It says nothing about reals that approximate slowly. The naive converse — that slow approximation implies algebraicity — is false at every p, since almost every real is transcendental with exponent exactly 2.

The bridge, and where the exponent actually lives

The sign expansion of a real is the greedy bisection: emit + when the current value undershoots \alpha, - otherwise. It provably brackets \alpha at every step, and once bracketed each further sign halves the bracket, giving

  \bigl\lvert \alpha - v_{n+k} \bigr\rvert \;\le\; \frac{\mathrm{gap}_n}{2^{k}} .

That rate alone certifies nothing. The error falls as 2^{-k} but the denominator grows as 2^{k} too, so it is approximation of exponent 1 — and every real is approximable to order 1 for free.

The exponent lives in the run structure. A + keeps the upper bound and raises the lower; a - does the reverse. So a run of k identical signs freezes one endpoint while the bracket keeps halving, leaving a rational fixed before the run began that approximates \alpha to accuracy 2^{-k} better:

  \Bigl\lvert \alpha - \frac{m}{2^{n}} \Bigr\rvert \;\le\; \frac{\mathrm{gap}_n}{2^{k}} ,

with the denominator pinned by the invariant that every bound after n steps is a dyadic over 2^n. Accuracy decouples from denominator, which is precisely what an approximation exponent above 1 means.

Measuring the run against n rather than absolutely turns this into an exponent: a run of length k \ge n t gives \lvert \alpha - m/2^n \rvert \le 1/(2^n)^t. And that closes the loop to the standard predicate —

  \Bigl(\text{runs of length } \ge n t \text{ for infinitely many } n\Bigr)
  \;\wedge\;
  \alpha \notin \mathbb{Q}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathrm{LiouvilleWith}\ t\ \alpha .

So the trajectory picture's central assertion — that run structure in the sign expansion controls the Diophantine exponent — is a proved implication. Irrationality is not a technicality here: a rational \alpha eventually is one of its own dyadic approximants, and the standard predicate excludes that case by definition.

⚠ The remaining input is a theorem, not a conjecture

What makes the criterion separate is Thue–Siegel–Roth: an algebraic irrational has approximation exponent exactly 2, hence is not approximable to any order p > 2. Granting that, "approximable to order 3" does what a separation must — it fails on every algebraic irrational and holds on an exhibited transcendental:

  \text{Roth}
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \Bigl(\ \forall\, \alpha \ \text{algebraic irrational},\ \ \neg\,\mathrm{LiouvilleWith}\,3\,\alpha \Bigr)
  \ \wedge\
  \mathrm{LiouvilleWith}\,3\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_{n} 2^{-n!}\Bigr).

The second conjunct is unconditional; the first is exactly Roth.

So this should not be recorded as an open conjecture. Roth proved it in 1955; it is a theorem, not an open problem — and the distinction matters here, because this conjecture has already carried three separate epistemic mislabelings: an "honest open state" that encoded nothing, a separation impossible as stated, and a direction already proved elsewhere.

⚠ A name collision makes the opposite error easy too. Searching a formal library for "Roth's theorem" succeeds — and returns the additive-combinatorics result on three-term arithmetic progressions, an unrelated theorem sharing the name. Thue–Siegel–Roth is absent, and a search by name says otherwise.

So the surreal side is not the obstacle, which is the opposite of what this conjecture's placement suggests. One genuine gap does remain on that side and should not be confused with the above: lifting any of this to birthday needs a per-step bound on \mathrm{birthday}(x/2), which the axioms neither supply nor imply.
conj:infinitesimal-frobenius:
Conjecture Infinitesimal Frobenius pairing: \int_A \circ \mu = \mathrm{id} + O(\varepsilon). Archimedean specialisation. The Frobenius axiom in quantum observable universe requires the pairing \int_A \circ \mu : A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} to induce an isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^{\vee} — a strict equality, hence a binary non-degeneracy condition. Over the surreals this condition can fail at infinitesimal scale, where a pairing may be non-degenerate only up to an infinitesimal correction. Two phenomena already invite such a reading — the diagonal regularisation of the Möbius energy and the small residual error in the QOU mass formula's \mathcal{Q}-values (quantified in §Significance below) — each of which the sections below interpret as an infinitesimal Frobenius deviation. In a surreal QOU, the strict axiom can accordingly be relaxed.

Conjecture

Let A be a Frobenius--Hopf object in a K-linear monoidal category with K = \mathbf{No}. The \varepsilon-relaxed Frobenius axiom is:

  (\int_A \circ \mu) \circ \eta_{A^\vee}
  \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} + \varepsilon \cdot \delta,

where \eta_{A^\vee} : A^\vee \to A \otimes A^\vee is the adjoint coevaluation, \varepsilon \in \mathbf{No} is a fixed positive infinitesimal, and \delta : A^\vee \to A^\vee is an arbitrary K-linear endomorphism (the deviation).

The conjecture asserts:

  1. Standard-part recovery: applying the standard-part map \mathrm{St} (standard-part map) to a relaxed Frobenius axiom yields a strict Frobenius axiom on the archimedean image. Concretely, \mathrm{St}(\delta) = 0 is automatic if and only if the deviation is birthday-shifted.

  2. Strict generalisation: there exist relaxed Frobenius structures with non-trivial deviation \delta (i.e. not gauge-equivalent to the strict structure) that nonetheless project to the same archimedean Frobenius structure.

If (2) holds, the relaxation is a strict generalisation of the classical Frobenius axiom, with the surreal QOU carrying first- order \varepsilon-corrections invisible to the archimedean QOU.

Plausibility

The classical Frobenius axiom \int \circ \mu = \mathrm{id} is a non-degeneracy condition. In a \mathbb{R}-linear category, this is binary (degenerate or not). In a \mathbf{No}-linear category, non-degeneracy can fail at infinitesimal scale: a pairing can have its Gram determinant equal to 1 + \varepsilon \cdot \delta rather than 1.

Whether such infinitesimal degeneracies are realisable (i.e. constructible from QOU axioms) is the content of (2). The natural candidate is to deform A by a coboundary at infinitesimal order:

  • pick a \delta \in \mathrm{End}(A^\vee);
  • define a new comultiplication \Delta_\varepsilon = \Delta + \varepsilon (\delta \otimes 1) \circ \Delta;
  • check that the Frobenius axiom is satisfied to order O(\varepsilon).

Whether the resulting structure is gauge-equivalent to the strict A is open.

Significance

Three uses:

  1. Möbius energy: the diagonal regularisation in the Möbius energy formula (Möbius energy proof) is accordingly read as an infinitesimal Frobenius deviation: the strict Frobenius axiom \int \delta(0) = infinity becomes \int \delta(\varepsilon) = 1/\varepsilon, and the regularised value is the standard-part.

  2. CODATA fits: the QOU mass formula's \sim 4\% MAE on \mathcal{Q}-values may be partly attributable to a small non-Frobenius deviation in the underlying algebra. An infinitesimal Frobenius axiom would absorb such deviations into a single \varepsilon-parameter.

  3. Mathematical interest: even without physical motivation, the relaxation gives a one-parameter deformation theory for Frobenius algebras, parallel to the classical Hochschild-cohomology obstruction theory but valued in \mathbf{No} rather than \mathbb{R}.

Proof strategy

The conjecture has two halves: standard-part recovery (easy) and strict generalisation (hard).

Standard-part recovery (provable now):

  1. Assume an \varepsilon-relaxed Frobenius algebra (A, \mu, \int_A, \delta) over \mathbf{No}.

  2. Apply \mathrm{St} to all components: \mathrm{St}(\delta) has coefficients in \mathbb{R}. Since \delta is multiplied by the infinitesimal \varepsilon, the term \varepsilon \cdot \delta is itself infinitesimal.

  3. Since \varepsilon \cdot \delta is infinitesimal, its standard part vanishes: \mathrm{St}(\varepsilon \cdot \delta) = 0. So \mathrm{St}((\int \circ \mu) \circ \eta) = \mathrm{St}(\mathrm{id} + \varepsilon \cdot \delta) = \mathrm{id}, recovering the strict Frobenius axiom.

Strict generalisation (open):

  1. Construct a candidate non-trivial \delta in a non-rigid Frobenius algebra. Concrete proposal: take A = \bigwedge^* V (exterior algebra) at infinitesimal q-deformation; the rigidity argument doesn't apply because \bigwedge^* V is not the regular representation.

  2. Verify the deformed pairing satisfies \int_\varepsilon \circ \mu_\varepsilon = \mathrm{id} + \varepsilon \cdot \delta for non-zero \delta.

  3. Show the deformed structure is not gauge-equivalent to the strict structure (a Hochschild-cohomology computation).

The two halves rest on very different prerequisites. Standard-part recovery needs only that the standard part of an infinitesimal vanishes and that it is additive — elementary facts about \mathrm{St}. Strict generalisation needs the Hochschild cohomology of Frobenius algebras over \mathbf{No}, a deformation theory over a surreal-coefficient field that has yet to be developed.

Falsification path: prove a rigidity theorem for \varepsilon-Frobenius algebras: every \varepsilon-deformation is gauge-equivalent to the strict structure. This would refute the strict-generalisation half by collapsing the relaxation.
conj:surreal-limit-transfer:
Conjecture Surreal limit transfer: limits as standard-part equalities via an \omega-evaluation. Archimedean specialisation. There is an \omega-evaluation \mathrm{ev}_\omega : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbf{No} of real sequences, sending constants to their embedded reals, respecting pointwise addition and multiplication, transferring eventual pointwise domination to the surreal order, and evaluating every convergent sequence infinitesimally close to its limit:

  a_n \to L
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) - L \in \mathfrak{m},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{st}\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_\omega(a)\bigr) = L .

Here \mathfrak{m} is the infinitesimal ideal of the finite valuation ring (valuation ring of finite surreals) and \mathrm{st} the standard-part map.

This is the block-level home for the "move analytic \to surreal" operation: an analytic limit statement becomes a surreal equality up to an infinitesimal — and, after \mathrm{st}, an exact equality. Two consequences are derived, fully proved, from the hypotheses of the conjecture:

  1. Limits are computed by \mathrm{st} \circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega .
  2. Limit comparison: if a_n \le b_n eventually and both converge, then \lim a_n \le \lim b_n — the eventual inequality is transferred to a single surreal inequality at \omega and the archimedean conclusion recovered by the proved monotonicity of \mathrm{st}. The classical strict-inequality collapse is visible structurally: \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) < \mathrm{ev}_\omega(b) is compatible with equal standard parts, so only \le survives the wall.

Epistemic status

The conjecture is stated as a precise hypothesis with no proof — it is open. For the concrete surreals the evaluation exists model-theoretically: Robinson's ultrapower supplies one [robinson1966], and the Berarducci–Mantova identification of surreals with transseries/germs [berarducci-mantova2018] supplies the canonical one for the definable-germ class (evaluation of the germ at \omega). Neither construction is available from the axiomatised surreal-field interface alone, which is exactly why the block is a conjecture rather than a theorem: what is conjectural is the compatibility package on the abstract interface, not the existence of some such map in set theory.

Relation to resummation

For a convergent sequence, \mathrm{st} \circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega is ordinary summation. For a divergent Gevrey-1 asymptotic series the same composite, applied to the Berarducci–Mantova evaluation of the associated transseries, is the median resummation — the identification recorded in st is median resummation. The conjecture is therefore the convergent-sector base case of the resummation dictionary: it fixes the normalisation that any median-resummation extension must restrict to.
conj:on-p-modular-hecke:
Conjecture Modular Hecke at q = \zeta_p corresponds to nimber surreals \mathbf{On}_p. Archimedean specialisation. This conjecture extends, to a primitive p-th root of unity, the char-0 surreal picture of Hecke representation theory recalled next. Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction identifies the binary \{L \mid R\} split at each Hecke eigenchannel step with Conway's recursive surreal construction. This works because the Hecke generator \sigma has exactly two eigenvalues at generic q.

At a primitive p-th root of unity q = \zeta_p, the representation theory of H_n(\zeta_p) acquires p-ary structure: when \geq p copies of the fundamental representation V are tensored, certain summands in the q-Schur--Weyl decomposition become trivial (Lusztig's small quantum group \mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) is finite-dimensional, with truncation governed by p).

This conjecture asserts the natural extension of Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction to the modular setting: the modular Hecke combinatorics at q = \zeta_p corresponds to nimber surreals \mathbf{On}_p in characteristic p (Lenstra--Conway).

Note on this paper

This conjecture is not load-bearing for QOU's main results; the aether value q_0 is generic (not a root of unity). The binary Hoefsmit / char-0 surreal picture applies throughout this paper. The char-p extension is included here as a conceptual companion. It records how the Hoefsmit machinery maps into the modular setting.

Background: nimber surreals

The nimber field \mathbf{On}_p is the field of all ordinals under:

  • nim-addition: \alpha \oplus \beta is the unique ordinal \gamma such that \gamma \neq \alpha' \oplus \beta for all \alpha' < \alpha and \gamma \neq \alpha \oplus \beta' for all \beta' < \beta. For finite ordinals in base p, this is digit-wise XOR-mod-p.
  • nim-multiplication: \alpha \otimes \beta defined recursively via the mex (minimum-excluded-value) operator.

For each prime p:

  • \mathbf{On}_2 is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, equal to the union of \mathbb{F}_{2^{2^k}} for all k (Conway, Lenstra).
  • \mathbf{On}_p for odd p is constructed analogously by Pruss and others.

These fields are the char-p analogues of \mathbf{No}: they form the algebraic-geometric ambient for ordinal-valued calculations in characteristic p, just as \mathbf{No} does in characteristic 0.

Conjecture

There is a p-ary analogue of the Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction bijection:

  \Phi_p :  \mathrm{KLcells}_n(\zeta_p)
   \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbf{On}_p^{[n]},

where:

  • \mathrm{KLcells}_n(\zeta_p) is the set of Kazhdan--Lusztig cells of H_n(\zeta_p) (which replace the Hoefsmit tableaux in the modular setting), and
  • \mathbf{On}_p^{[n]} is the set of nimbers of p-adic depth \leq n (analogous to dyadic surreals of birthday \leq n).

The bijection \Phi_p is determined by the p-ary fusion data: at each step, a vector decomposes into p eigencomponents (rather than 2) according to the cyclic-group action of \mathbb{Z}/p on the truncated tensor power.

The smallest instance already makes this correspondence concrete: at p = 2, n = 3 the three Kazhdan--Lusztig cells of H_3(-1) are conjectured to match the first three nimbers 0, 1, *2 (worked out in the proof strategy below).

Surviving and broken structure

Compared to the char-0 surreal lift (algebraic core survives):

See Table.

The crucial break is Wedderburn semisimplicity: at q = \zeta_p the Hecke algebra is not semisimple, so the Hoefsmit-style diagonalisation fails. The replacement is the Kazhdan--Lusztig cell decomposition, which is p-ary rather than binary.

Visibility in characteristic 0

The p-ary structure at q = \zeta_p is not purely modular — it is visible in characteristic 0 as the limit behaviour of the Hecke algebra near roots of unity. Specifically:

  • Dixmier--Lusztig truncation: at generic q, every tensor power V^{\otimes n} has \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 summands (binary Hoefsmit tree). At q = \zeta_p, summands with \dim_q(\lambda) = 0 disappear; the surviving summands are reorganised into p-cycles.

  • Quantum trivialisation: when exactly p copies of V at q = \zeta_p are tensored, the trivial representation acquires multiplicity p (or 0, depending on parity), instead of 1. This is the "p braids coming together" — p strands fuse into a single quantum-trivial channel.

  • Fusion ring: the truncated tensor product \otimes_{\zeta_p} on \mathrm{Rep}(\mathfrak{u}_{\zeta_p}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) has p-1 simple objects with p-ary fusion rules. The fusion graph is the Dynkin diagram A_{p-1}, generalising the binary A_1 of generic Hecke.

In QOU specifically, the golden-ratio degeneration at q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 (golden-ratio degeneration, if present) is the p = 5 case: the Descartes elliptic curve nodes at \zeta_5, and Hecke fusion becomes 5-ary.

Implications for QOU

If the conjecture holds, QOU has a parallel theory in characteristic p for each prime p:

  • QOU_{\mathbf{No}}: the surreal lift over \mathbf{No} (this appendix).
  • QOU_{\mathbf{On}_p}: the modular lift over \mathbf{On}_p, one for each prime p.

The two lifts are related by:

  • both reduce to the same archimedean QOU when "evaluated at q = q_0" (in the sense of the standard-part for char 0; in some analogous sense for char p);
  • they record different kinds of fine structure (infinitesimal-corrections in char 0 vs. p-ary fusion data in char p);
  • they are both valid algebraic ambients for the same underlying \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]-form of QOU.

Speculative physical readings of the char-p lifts are not pursued here. The mathematical content — that modular Hecke at \zeta_p corresponds to \mathbf{On}_p surreals — is the actual claim.

Proof strategy

The conjecture's two halves: nimber existence (mathematically established) and Hecke \leftrightarrow nimber correspondence (open).

Layer 1: nimber field existence (cited):

  1. \mathbf{On}_2 is constructed by Conway–Lenstra [conway1976] as the union of \mathbb{F}_{2^{2^k}}; algebraically closed, characteristic 2.

  2. \mathbf{On}_p for odd p: similar construction via nim-arithmetic. Established in the algebraic-geometry literature.

Layer 2: Hecke-cell \leftrightarrow nimber bijection (open):

  1. Smallest case (p = 2, n = 3): compute the Kazhdan–Lusztig cells of H_3(\zeta_2) = H_3(-1) explicitly. H_3(-1) has 3 cells: \{1\}, \{\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\}, and \{\sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1\} (with appropriate W-graph structure).

  2. Match against the first 3 elements of \mathbf{On}_2: the nim-numbers 0, 1, *2 (where *2 is the third nimber, equal to the surreal \{0,1 \mid \}).

  3. Verify that the bijection respects the \mathbb{Z}/2 action (Frobenius / sign symmetry).

  4. Generalise to larger n and other primes p by induction on KL-cell complexity.

Falsification path: produce a H_n(\zeta_p)-cell that does not correspond to any nimber of depth \leq n (i.e., a "phantom" cell with no nimber witness). Such an example would require p-ary fusion data not captured by nim-arithmetic, suggesting a different combinatorial replacement is needed.

Provability assessment: Layer 1 already established. Layer 2 for p = 2, n = 3 is feasible by hand — a matter of weeks. General Layer 2 requires Kazhdan–Lusztig cell theory, a substantial multi-year project.

conj:os-reflection-positivity-from-reeb:
Conjecture Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2. Recovering an Osterwalder--Schrader Euclidean field theory from the q-deformed aether requires reflection positivity of the categorical correlation pairings. This conjecture posits that the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2 acting on the Frobenius pairing furnishes Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity in the archimedean realisation.

Conjecture (OS reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2). Let \theta denote the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset U(1)_{\xi} inside the Reeb U(1)—equivalently, the chart-swap involution \iota : Z \mapsto Z^{-1} on the contact affine chart at \varTheta = \pi, per chart-swap U(1) is the Reeb flow. Then the Frobenius pairing \langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_F on A satisfies reflection positivity under \theta:

\langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F \geq 0 \qquad \text{for every state } \phi \in A_+,

with equality if and only if \phi vanishes on the positive-time half of the Reeb decomposition. Under the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, this categorical positivity descends to the Osterwalder–Schrader reflection-positivity axiom of the four Euclidean Wightman correlation functions \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\langle \phi_1 \cdots \phi_n \rangle_F\bigr) on the \varepsilon \to 0 standard manifold \mathbb{R}^4.

The Osterwalder–Schrader reflection \theta_{\mathrm{OS}} on Euclidean spacetime is reflection in the \tau = 0 hyperplane, i.e., (x_1, x_2, x_3, \tau) \mapsto (x_1, x_2, x_3, -\tau). In the categorical contact-geometric formulation, Euclidean time is the Reeb parameter t along \xi (categorical Reeb derivation), so \theta_{\mathrm{OS}} acts on the contact affine chart as \phi_t \mapsto \phi_{-t}. The categorical realisation of this involution is precisely the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup at \varTheta = \pi of the chart-swap U(1) family \rho_\varTheta : z \mapsto e^{i\varTheta} z. The chart-swap–Reeb identification shows this coincides with the Reeb flow U(1). No separate OS reflection needs to be constructed: it is already present in the categorical infrastructure as the \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup of the Reeb circle.

The Frobenius pairing is governed by the Nakayama automorphism \nu \in \mathrm{Aut}(A): \langle a, b \rangle_F = \langle b, \nu(a) \rangle_F, while the sesquilinear \ast-pairing \langle X, Y \rangle_{\tau,\ast} = \tau(X^\dagger Y) is hermitian (\langle X, Y \rangle_{\tau,\ast} = \overline{\langle Y, X \rangle_{\tau,\ast}}) on the radical quotient A / \mathrm{rad}\,\tau. Under the \theta-action on A, the antipode S swaps the two factors and inverts the Reeb flow direction. Hermiticity of the \ast-twisted Frobenius pairing implies \theta-compatibility up to the Reeb-half decomposition. The conjecture is the positivity statement: for any state \phi supported on the positive-time Reeb half, \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F evaluates to a non-negative scalar in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}). Hermiticity alone makes \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F real, without forcing the real value to be non-negative. The required structural input is that the antipode-twisted pairing \langle \theta(\cdot), \cdot \rangle_F descends through \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to a positive-definite inner product on the half-line L^2(\mathbb{R}_{>0}).

The Osterwalder–Schrader theorem states that a family of Euclidean correlation functions \{S_n\} on \mathbb{R}^4 defines a Wightman QFT on Minkowski space if and only if (OS0) temperedness, (OS1) Euclidean covariance, (OS2) reflection positivity, (OS3) symmetry, and (OS4) cluster decomposition all hold.

In the QOU framework:

OS0 (temperedness) \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} images of partial products \Phi_n are tempered by the archimedean limit conjecture at every x \in (0, 1).
OS1 (Euclidean covariance) S_5-action on Bring's coordinate ring is the categorical lift of the \mathrm{SO}(4) / \mathrm{Spin}(4) rotation group, and the \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow U(1)_{\xi} hierarchy is the Euclidean time translation.

OS2 is the open structural input isolated by this conjecture: whether the antipode-twisted Frobenius pairing descends under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to a reflection-positive Euclidean inner product.

The positivity statement involves three open ingredients:

  1. Categorical positivity of the antipode-twisted pairing. The Frobenius pairing is constructively non-degenerate, but neither the QOU axioms nor the Frobenius–Hopf aether definition currently impose positivity of \langle \theta(\cdot), \cdot \rangle_F. The conjecture claims the aether, being a C^*-Frobenius–Hopf algebra in the archimedean specialisation (q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}), inherits positivity from the C^*-norm.
  2. Stability under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. The archimedean realisation functor must commute with the positivity restriction: \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\langle\theta(\phi),\phi\rangle_F\bigr) = \bigl\langle\theta_{\mathrm{OS}}\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\phi),\, \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\phi)\bigr\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^4)}. Equivalently, the OS reflection on the standard Euclidean correlation functions is the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the Reeb antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 action. This follows from the chart-swap–Reeb identification once \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} preserves the U(1)_{\xi}-action on contact charts.
  3. Supporting infrastructure. A complete proof requires a Frobenius structure on the categorical C^*-completion together with the Wightman reconstruction theorem. The conjecture amounts to a single positivity inequality; granting it, the surreal bound completes OS reconstruction.

Ingredients (2) and (3) are technical plumbing once the categorical content is settled. The only genuinely new mathematical input needed is a single positivity axiom on the aether Frobenius algebra. A Frobenius algebra (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon) in a C^*-tensor category is positive if its evaluation map \eta : \mathbf{1} \to A admits a state-positive lift—i.e., the composition

\mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\;\eta\;} A \xrightarrow{\;\Delta\;} A \otimes A \xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{id}\,\otimes\,*\;} A \otimes A^*

factors through the positive cone of A \otimes A^*. The missing input is exactly this:

Axiom (aether C^*-Frobenius positivity). At the archimedean aether value q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}, the Frobenius–Hopf aether A admits a C^*-completion in which the unit map \eta : \mathbf{1} \to A is positive in the categorical sense above. Equivalently, (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon) is a positive Frobenius algebra in the C^*-tensor category \mathbf{C} at q_0.

Granting the aether C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom, along with Chart-swap U(1) equals the Reeb U(1) as subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}(V)) and Archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}, OS axiom (OS2) holds: \langle\theta(\phi), \phi\rangle_F \geq 0 for every state \phi in the positive-time Reeb half.

The proof sketch involves three steps:

  1. Categorical reflection = Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2. By Chart-swap U(1) equals the Reeb U(1) as subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}(V)), \theta is the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset T_q subgroup acting on the contact-affine chart \mathbb{P}(V) via z \mapsto -z. On the aether Hopf algebra A, the action \theta_A : A \to A factors through the antipode S via the T_q-grading: \theta_A = S \circ (\mathrm{sign}\,\text{of}\,\xi\text{-grading}).
  2. Antipode-twisted pairing = state-positive form. The aether Frobenius pairing factors through the antipode by \langle a, b \rangle_F = \varepsilon(\mu(a, S(b))). Composing with \theta_A: \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F = \varepsilon(\mu(\theta(\phi), S(\phi))) = \varepsilon(\mu(S(\phi^*), S(\phi))) where \phi^* is the C^*-conjugate. By the aether positivity axiom, this evaluates to a non-negative element of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}) = k.
  3. Stability under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} sends the categorical C^*-norm to the standard L^2-norm on \mathbb{R}^4 by construction. Positivity is preserved.

The status of OS reflection positivity in the QOU framework is equal to the status of this single C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom. The axiom is well-formulated inside unitary fusion categories and unitary C^*-Frobenius algebras. Verifying that the QOU aether A at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} satisfies it requires:

  • A choice of C^*-norm on A compatible with the q_0-deformation.
  • Verification that one of these candidate norms makes the Frobenius pairing positive in the sense above.
  • Compatibility of the chosen norm with the antipode S.

The Euclidean reflection-positivity condition in the QOU model reduces to structural positivity of the antipode-twisted Frobenius pairing. The reflection involved is the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup of the Reeb U(1), made visible by the chart-swap–Reeb identification.
conj:wenzl-positivity-implies-aether-pos:
Conjecture Wenzl positivity at q_0 implies aether C^*-Frobenius positivity. Archimedean specialisation. The companion conjecture Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2 isolates a single aether hypothesis for Euclidean reflection positivity: C^*-Frobenius positivity of the QOU Frobenius--Hopf aether at q = q_0. This conjecture posits that this hypothesis is derivable from Wenzl's positivity criterion for \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}.

Conjecture (Wenzl positivity at q_0 implies aether C^*-Frobenius positivity). Wenzl's positivity criterion for the representation category \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) at q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} — the criterion that picks out unitary fusion categories among the q-deformed semisimple ones — implies the aether C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom of Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2. Equivalently, the Müger C^*-norm on the Frobenius–Hopf aether A at q_0, induced by the categorical trace of \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)), makes the antipode-twisted Frobenius pairing \langle\theta(\cdot), \cdot\rangle_F positive-definite on the positive-time Reeb half.

Here \theta is the Reeb reflection (the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset U(1) of Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2) and \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_F the Frobenius form of A.

The natural follow-up

The OS-reflection-positivity conjecture Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2 leaves the aether C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom as the sole genuinely new input. That axiom has three free parameters:

  1. Choice of C^*-norm on A at q_0. The aether algebra A at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} admits several candidate C^*-completions:
    • the universal C^*-norm of A as a *-algebra;
    • the GNS norm with respect to the Frobenius pairing;
    • the Müger norm built from the categorical trace of the ambient tensor category.
  2. Positivity of the antipode-twisted pairing in the chosen norm.
  3. Compatibility with the antipode S.

The Müger norm has properties (2) and (3) by construction for any unitary C^*-tensor category \mathbf{C} in the BKLR sense (Müger 2003, Bischoff–Kawahigashi–Longo–Rehren). The only open question is therefore whether \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} is unitary as a C^*-tensor category. That is exactly the content of Wenzl's positivity criterion.

Wenzl's criterion (recall)

Wenzl proved ([wenzl1988], [wenzl1990], with the \mathrm{SU}(N) generalisation by Wenzl and the \mathfrak{sl}_n-equivariant version by Kazhdan–Wenzl [kazhdanwenzl1993]): the representation category \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) admits a unitary structure (positive C^*-trace + positive inner product on each Hom space) iff q lies in either:

  • \{q = e^{i\pi / N} : N \geq 3\} (the roots-of-unity range yielding the modular tensor categories at level N - 2); or
  • \{q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}\} (the real positive range, in particular q_0 \approx 1.10998).

The criterion is sharp: outside these two regions, the categorical trace fails to be positive, and no C^*-completion of the underlying algebra makes \mathrm{Rep} a C^*-tensor category.

The QOU aether parameter q_0 \approx 1.10998 lies in the second region (real positive). Wenzl's criterion therefore applies, and \mathrm{Rep}(U_{q_0}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) is unitary. By the standard Müger / BKLR theory, every Frobenius algebra in a unitary C^*-tensor category is automatically a positive Frobenius algebra (in the sense of the aether axiom of Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2).

The conjecture's actual claim

The conjecture is therefore the identification step between two positivity notions:

(a) Wenzl-positivity of \mathrm{Rep}(U_{q_0}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) as a C^*-tensor category — established. (b) Aether C^*-Frobenius positivity of (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon) as a Frobenius algebra in \mathrm{Rep}(U_{q_0}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) — needed by Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2.

(a) is a theorem; (b) is the aether axiom, so the conjecture is exactly the claim that (a) implies (b) via the categorical Frobenius–algebra theory of Müger / BKLR.

Structural role

If this conjecture holds, Euclidean reflection positivity of the categorical Frobenius pairing at q_0 follows from:

  • Chart-swap U(1) equals the Reeb U(1) as subgroups of \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}(V)) — chart-swap U(1) is the Reeb U(1);
  • Wenzl positivity at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} [wenzl1988];
  • Müger / BKLR positive-Frobenius theory;
  • This bridge conjecture identifying the induced C^*-Frobenius structure on A.

Unitarity is compatible with q = q_0, but it does not single q_0 out. Wenzl's unitarity range is the whole real positive line, so every q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} satisfies it equally. The value of q_0 is fixed by the weak-modulus aether calibration, not by unitarity.
sec:surreal-appendix-conclusion:
Open questions and outlook.

The surreal-number lift of QOU raises several questions:

  1. Surreal measure? The category \mathbf{No} carries no canonical Lebesgue measure. Loeb-type constructions on hyperfinite subsets of \mathbf{No} yield finitely additive measures that pull back to \mathbb{R} under the standard part. Whether such a construction recovers the Frobenius integral \int_A up to an infinitesimal is left open.
  2. Surreal Hilbert-like object. The scattering pipeline's Hilbert space \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phys}} lacks a surreal analogue with a canonical inner product. Whether a birthday-bounded completion yields a weaker surrogate—sufficient for the mass formula but lacking spectral theory—remains to be investigated.
  3. Categorical size. Since \mathbf{No} is a proper class, defining \mathbf{Mod}_{\mathbf{No}} or \mathbf{Rep}_{\mathbf{No}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) requires universe-polymorphic foundations or restriction to a set-sized Hahn-series sub-field. This is sidestepped by stating axioms over a fixed real-closed field K extending \mathbb{R}.
  4. Genuine generalisations. The strict QOU axioms (\int \circ \eta = \mathrm{id}, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0) might force the \varepsilon-relaxed versions to coincide with the strict ones in any rigid monoidal category. If so, the \varepsilon-flexibility is illusory.
  5. Kashaev as a surreal statement. The reformulation \mathrm{st}\bigl(2 \pi \log |J_K(q_\omega, \omega)|/\omega\bigr) = \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) (Kashaev surreal) is equivalent to the classical conjecture, modulo the meaning of q_\omega. It separates the algebraic (Hecke/Markov) content from the transcendental (dilogarithm, hyperbolic volume) content.

Accomplishments of this appendix:

  • An explicit ambient for the q \to 1 limit and renormalisation blow-ups, avoiding informal \infty notation.
  • An isomorphism between the Hoefsmit seminormal form (central to the mass formula) and Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction.
  • A disciplined framework for \varepsilon-relaxed axioms.
  • A catalogue of which QOU constructions are purely algebraic (hence field-polymorphic) versus genuinely analytic.

This appendix serves as raw material for future work rather than a completed extension of the theory.
prose:formalisation-coverage:
Every proof in this paper possesses a corresponding Lean 4 formalisation, except where explicitly citing external references for large prior results. 725 of 730 (99.3%) provable claims (theorems, lemmas, propositions, corollaries) carry full Lean proofs; the remainder bear the sorry marker against an explicit bibliographic reference. The paper poses 106 primary open conjectures of its own—famous external open problems it connects to, and conjectures conditional on those primaries, are tallied separately—of which 77 (72.6%) are class-axiomatised in Lean using the conditional-class convention. This allows downstream results to persist as fully verified conditional theorems. The Lean sources reside at https://github.com/litlfred/qou.

Four-tier formalisation architecture

Across approximately 4{,}850 Lean 4 modules under QOU/, formalised declarations are stratified into a strict four-tier directed acyclic graph so that reusable pure mathematics never depends on physical interpretations or numerical constants:

  1. Tier 0 — Mathlib4 foundation. Commutative algebra, monoidal and rigid categories, representation theory, algebraic topology, measure theory, and analytic special functions imported directly from Mathlib.
  2. Tier A — Mathlib4 core upstreaming additions (QOU/MathlibExt/). General-purpose theorems filling immediate upstream library gaps—including the unit group \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]^\times = \{\pm q^m\}, the Clausen and Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm pentagon identities, and piecewise-linear link isotopy—designed to drop directly into existing Mathlib namespaces.
  3. Tier B — Six standalone Reservoir community libraries (QOU/MathlibInfra/, QOU/HeckeAlgebra/, QOU/Nuclear/). Self-contained pure-mathematics packages covering Iwahori--Hecke and Temperley--Lieb towers, Nakayama-twisted Frobenius--Hopf algebras, generic-ordered-ring conic duality and toric Gröbner bases, finite Rieffel compact quantum metric spaces, Thomae--Jackson q-calculus, and Artin braid / Bring surface / octonionic colour geometry.
  4. Tier C — QOU categorical core and Archimedean boundary (QOU/QuantumUniverse/, QOU/Torsion/, QOU/Archimedean/). Pre-wall categorical constructions over arbitrary commutative rings R (|q| > 1 or q \in R^\times), separated explicitly from the post-wall real comparison layer at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}.

Kernel trust and non-vacuity discipline

Every closed theorem in Tiers A--C satisfies three mechanical verification invariants:

  • Standard kernel axioms only. Inspecting the kernel axiom footprint of any complete theorem yields at most Lean's three standard foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Zero custom axiom declarations are permitted anywhere in the formalisation.
  • Explicit typeclass packaging of open hypotheses. Unproved mathematical or physical conjectures are encoded as explicit Lean class or structure parameters rather than global axioms, ensuring that every downstream theorem displays its exact conditional dependencies in its type signature.
  • Automated non-vacuity auditing. A four-rule syntactic and semantic vacuity gate scans every module for self-assuming hypotheses, tautological typeclass field projections, conjunction projections, and direct hypothesis rewrites, preventing vacuous wrappers from masquerading as substantive derivations.

prop:bloch-group-quotient-construction:
Proposition Concrete construction of B(F) as the free abelian quotient by the pentagon subgroup (closes substantive Mathlib gap 1).

The Bloch group BlochGroup F for a field-like type F admits a concrete Lean construction as the quotient

  B(F) \;:=\; \mathrm{FreeAbelianGroup}\bigl(\mathrm{PreBlochElement}\,F\bigr)
            \;\big/\; \mathrm{pentagonSubgroup},

where PreBlochElement F carries the pre-Bloch elements (val ≠ 0 and val ≠ 1) and pentagonSubgroup is the AddSubgroup.closure of the five-term pentagon-relation generators. The quotient inherits an AddCommGroup structure from the QuotientAddGroup instance in Mathlib. It carries a canonical projection quot : PreBlochGroup F →+ BlochGroup F and satisfies the standard universal property.

See Table for the Lean structure.

This construction yields a genuine AddCommGroup rather than a typeclass ansatz. The carrier types admit a real Lean construction. The HasBlochGroup ℝ instance is concretely inhabited.

The unconstrained PentagonShape F accepts arbitrary five-tuples of pre-Bloch elements. This makes pentagonRelationGenerators too permissive. Degenerate shapes with repeated entries trivialize the quotient. A ValidPentagonShape F predicate must constrain PentagonShape F to enforce the Rogers-form constraints:

  e_3 \;\equiv\; e_2 / e_1, \quad
  e_4 \;\equiv\; (1 - e_2^{-1})/(1 - e_1^{-1}), \quad
  e_5 \;\equiv\; (1 - e_2)/(1 - e_1).

These constraints derive from a valid Rogers pair (x, y) \in F^\times \times F^\times with x \neq y, x \neq 0, x \neq 1, y \neq 0, and y \neq 1. This derivation requires decidability of the pentagon-domain conditions on F, a pentagon-shape map F \times F \to \mathrm{PentagonShape}\,F, and the restriction of pentagonRelationGenerators to the ValidPentagonShape F subtype. The structural skeleton accommodates this restriction via the validity predicate and the constrained range.

The conditional-class chain anchored by prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness brings BlochSuslinUniqueness closer to unconditional inhabitation. The remaining work includes the pentagon identity proof for \mathrm{Cl}_2 on the unit-circle subset, Bloch-Wigner regulator D \otimes \mathbb{Q} injectivity, and the Suslin map K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}.
